headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and distribution infrastructure onto large energy users, such as data centers, to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Senator L. Louise Lucas, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Clean Virginia, environmental advocates, residential ratepayers, Dominion Energy (with amendments).
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business or utility groups concerned about permitting delays and added costs.
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills Shifting Data Center Costs to Users
news_summary: Governor Spanberger amended HB 1393 and SB 253, which aim to transfer energy costs for new distribution infrastructure and capacity auction prices onto high-load users like data centers. The amendments removed an opt-out for facilities under construction and gave the SCC more authority to reject unreasonable projects, ultimately aiming to save residential customers money.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandated
short_summary: This bill requires water users supplying data centers to report monthly or quarterly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for increased transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Joshua Thomas, Delegate Sam Rasoul, environmental and conservation groups, Piedmont Environmental Council, community advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (implied, as they often prefer less transparency).
news_headline: Virginia Bill Increases Data Center Water Reporting Requirements
news_summary: Senate Bill 553, now awaiting the governor's signature, increases reporting requirements for data centers regarding their water consumption. This legislation aims to bring transparency to data center water usage, a growing concern for communities and environmental advocates in Virginia.

headline: Local Control Over Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill empowers localities to require site assessments for new high-energy data centers, including noise studies and evaluations of impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Joshua Thomas, Delegate Sam Rasoul, environmental and conservation groups, neighborhood and parent associations, historic preservation advocates, farmland protection groups, local planning and public health organizations.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business or utility groups concerned about permitting delays and added costs.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Mandates Data Center Siting Impact Assessments
news_summary: HB 153, passed by the legislature, establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise near homes and schools. It also allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources, giving local governments more control over data center development.
